title: G. Saraswathi vs G. Narasimha Rao on 4 July, 2023

paragraphs.text:
ITEM NO.1 COURT NO.11 SECTION XVI-A

 S U P R E M E C O U R T O F I N D I A
 RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS

 CONTEMPT PETITION (CIVIL) NO. 745/2022
 IN
 TRANSFER PETITION (CIVIL) NO. 404/2020

 G. SARASWATHI Petitioner(s)

 VERSUS

 G. NARASIMHA RAO Respondent(s)

 (NOT TO BE DELETED FROM 04.07.2023 AS BAILABLE WARRANTS ISSUED
 REQUIRING THE RESPONDENT TO BE PERSONALLY PRESENT ON 04.07.2023
 BEFORE THE HON'BLE COURT)

 Date : 04-07-2023 This petition was called on for hearing today.

 CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE HRISHIKESH ROY
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PANKAJ MITHAL

 For Petitioner(s) Mr. Tanvir Nayar, AOR

 For Respondent(s) Ms. Prerna Robin, Adv.
 Mr. B. Shravanth Shanker, AOR
 Mr. B Yeshwanth Raj, Adv.

 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following

 O R D E R

1. Heard Mr. Tanvir Nayar, learned counsel, who is appearing

 together with the petitioner. Also heard Ms. Prerna Robin, learned

 counsel, who is appearing together with the respondent.

2. This contempt proceeding is initiated alleging non-compliance

 of the following two conditions recorded in the settlement

 agreement dated 08.12.2021:

“(i) That both the parties agree and undertake to file the
Signature Not Verified
 Divorce Petition by mutual consent under Section 10A of
Digitally signed by
NITIN TALREJA
Date: 2023.07.06
 Divorce Act, 1869 or under Section 28 of the Special
15:04:17 IST
Reason: Marriage Act 1954, as applicable, before the Principal
 Family Judge, Family Courts, Patiala House Courts, New


 1
 Delhi on or before 15.04.2022. Both the parties undertake
 to be present before the appropriate Court for filing and
 for recording of the statements in the mutual consent
 divorce petition.

4. It has been agreed between the parties that
 Respondent-husband Mr. G. Narasimha Rao shall pay a sum of
 Rs.8,00,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakh Only) as full and final
 settlement to Mrs. G. Saraswathi @ Pokuri Saraswati
 towards her Stridhan if any, her maintenance past,
 present, future and permanent Alimony and towards
 maintenance of their child namely G. Madhumeeta. The
 Respondent-husband has agreed to provide a copy of his
 Aadhaar Card for the benefit and use of child G.
 Madhumeeta.”

3. On the above, Ms. Prerna Robin, the learned counsel submits

that the respondent had a mishap and therefore, he could arrange

only Rs. 3 lakhs (Rupees Three Lakhs Only) but is prepared to pay

the balance Rs. 5 lakhs (Rupees Five Lakhs Only) within two months,

if this is permitted by the Court. Insofar as the joint

application for divorce to be filed by mutual consent under Section

10A of the Divorce Act, 1869 is concerned, it is submitted that let

the financial transactions be completed and then the joint

application can be filed by both parties.

4. Taking note of the above, the cheque for a sum of Rs. 3 lakhs

(Rupees Three Lakhs Only) bearing No. 223091 dated 04.07.2023

(State Bank of India) is noted to be handed over by the respondent

to the petitioner in the Court itself. The balance Rs. 5 lakhs

(Rupees Five Lakhs Only) would be payable by 06.09.2023.

(NITIN TALREJA) (KAMLESH RAWAT)
COURT MASTER (SH) ASSISTANT REGISTRAR
